fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of my work has been building machine learning and full-stack systems for real users. Right now I work on the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I own large parts of the data and ML infrastructure: the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection microservice and CI scaffold, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer for prioritizing alerts. I also built a retrieval-augmented explanation layer, because an anomaly system that floods analysts with alerts creates a second problem instead of solving the first. Before that I worked with Intelehealth on AI and data systems for rural telemedicine, including a Python resource-availability scoring pipeline across 32 villages and an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard. I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence and built ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app in Swift/SwiftUI with passive sleep estimation from HealthKit and Core Motion signals, shipped into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users.
